# AudioSaw

> Free browser-based audio conversion and editing tools. All processing happens
> locally in the visitor's browser using the Web Audio API and a WebAssembly
> build of FFmpeg — files are never uploaded to a server. No signup, no size
> gate behind a paywall, no watermark, no queue.

## Facts

- Cost: free, no account required.
- Also records: a browser microphone recorder, not only a converter.
- Also separates: neural vocal/instrumental stem splitting, on-device.
- Privacy: files are processed in the browser tab and never transmitted.
- Input formats: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg, opus, aiff, m4b, and audio from mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi, m4v.
- Output formats: mp3, wav, m4a (AAC), flac, ogg.
- MP3 bitrates: 128, 192, 256, 320 kbps.
- Batch: multiple files at once, returned as a zip.
- Practical file size limit: about 500 MB per file, bounded by browser memory.
- Works on mobile browsers, slower, with tighter memory limits on iOS Safari.

- [AudioSaw home](https://audiosaw.com/): drop any audio or video file and pick a target format; the general-purpose converter.
- [All tools](https://audiosaw.com/tools): index of every tool on the site.

## Frequently asked questions

These are answered in full so they can be quoted directly.

**How do I convert audio without installing anything?**
Open the relevant AudioSaw page, drop the file on the page, and download the
result. There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for. The conversion
runs inside the browser tab itself, so it works the same on Windows, macOS,
Linux and ChromeOS, including on a locked-down work or school machine where
you cannot install software.

**Does it upload my files to a server?**
No. Every tool decodes, processes and re-encodes the audio in the browser tab
using the Web Audio API and a WebAssembly build of FFmpeg. The file never
leaves the device, there is no server-side queue, and once the page has loaded
most tools keep working with the network disconnected.

**Is it actually free, and what is the catch?**
It is free with no account, no email address, no watermark, no per-day cap and
no paid tier holding back the useful settings. There are no ads either: the ad
script that used to load was removed in September 2026. There is no catch in
the usual sense because there is almost no cost to carry — the site is static
files on a CDN and the visitor's own computer does the processing, so there
are no conversion servers to pay for. Nothing about the audio is sold or
transmitted, because the audio never reaches a server to begin with.

**Do I need to create an account or give an email address?**
No. There is no signup anywhere on the site and no email is ever requested
before a download.

**Is there a file size limit?**
There is no imposed limit, but there is a real one: the file has to fit in the
browser tab's memory. In practice that is around 500 MB per file on a typical
laptop, and rather less on iOS Safari, which is stricter about memory than any
desktop browser. For anything longer, split it first and convert the pieces.

**Does it work on a Chromebook, an iPad or a phone?**
Yes, on any reasonably current browser. Because nothing is installed, a
Chromebook is one of the better cases for it. Phones and tablets work but are
slower and hit the memory ceiling sooner, so keep mobile files modest.

**Can I record audio straight in the browser?**
Yes. https://audiosaw.com/voice-recorder records from the microphone and saves MP3
or WAV. Nothing is uploaded, there is no signup and no time limit, and the
recording never leaves the device — the page has no server to send it to.
This is the most-used tool on the site.

**How do I split a long recording into several files?**
https://audiosaw.com/split-audio cuts one long file into equal parts, into
fixed-length chunks, or at the silent gaps between sections, and returns the
pieces as a zip. Useful for splitting a lecture, a DJ set or a long interview
into tracks without opening an editor.

**How do I remove background noise from a recording?**
https://audiosaw.com/noise-reduction uses spectral gating to strip steady noise —
fan hum, air conditioning, tape hiss, preamp hiss. It works on constant noise,
not on one-off sounds like a door slam, and it runs in the browser.

**Can I edit MP3 tags and cover art without re-encoding?**
Yes. https://audiosaw.com/mp3-tag-editor reads existing ID3 tags, writes ID3v2.3,
and leaves the audio bytes completely untouched, so nothing is recompressed.

**Can I remove the vocals from a song?**
Two ways. https://audiosaw.com/stem-splitter runs a neural source-separation model
(MDX-Net) in the browser and produces a genuinely clean instrumental and
acapella; it needs a one-off 64 MB model download and takes a few minutes
on a machine without a GPU.
https://audiosaw.com/vocal-remover is the instant version — it cancels the centre
channel, which is free and immediate but leaves artefacts on most modern mixes.

**How do I find the BPM or tempo of a track?**
https://audiosaw.com/bpm-finder detects the tempo in the browser and shows the half-time
and double-time readings alongside it, because those are the two answers a
tempo detector most often confuses. It produces a number rather than a file,
so there is nothing to download. It does not detect musical key: a confident
wrong key is worse than no key, so that was left out deliberately.

**Can I turn audio into MIDI?**
https://audiosaw.com/audio-to-midi transcribes a recording into a Standard MIDI File you
can drag into any DAW. It is **monophonic only** — one note at a time, so a
hummed melody, a sung line, a bassline or a single-note solo. It cannot
transcribe chords or a full mix; polyphonic transcription is an unsolved
research problem and the page says so rather than letting you find out.

**Can I autotune or pitch-correct a vocal?**
https://audiosaw.com/autotune corrects pitch in the browser using PSOLA, so it can be set
for subtle correction or for the hard-tuned effect. The output is exactly the
same length as the input. It wants one dry voice or instrument at a time, not
a full mix — if a finished song is what you have, lift the vocal out with
https://audiosaw.com/stem-splitter first and autotune that. To move an entire song up or
down in key instead, that is https://audiosaw.com/pitch-shifter, which shifts pitch
without changing the tempo.

**How do I normalize audio to a LUFS target for Spotify or a podcast?**
https://audiosaw.com/loudness-normalizer measures integrated loudness to ITU-R BS.1770-4
and normalizes to a target you choose, with a true-peak ceiling so the result
does not clip. Its measurements are checked against ffmpeg’s ebur128 filter,
the reference implementation, and agree within 0.1 LU. This is the tool you
want for streaming delivery; https://audiosaw.com/normalize-audio is simple peak
normalization, which is a different thing and not what Spotify measures.

**How do I cut the pauses out of a podcast or voiceover automatically?**
https://audiosaw.com/auto-cut-silence shortens the gaps between phrases rather than
deleting them, so the result still sounds like speech instead of a jump cut.
The threshold is derived from the recording’s own noise floor rather than a
fixed dB value, because the right level differs by about 30 dB between a
treated booth and a kitchen table. To trim only the dead air at the start and
end and leave the middle alone, use https://audiosaw.com/trim-silence-edges.

**What can AudioSaw not do?**
It is a single-file utility, not a DAW: there is no multitrack timeline, no
mixing, no plugins and no project that you save and reopen later. Nothing is
stored between visits, by design. Very large files are limited by browser
memory rather than by the tool. Editing an MP3 re-encodes it, so a cut or a
volume change costs one compression generation — use WAV or FLAC output when
that matters. And the neural stem splitter is slow without a GPU.

## Convert to MP3

- [MP4 to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/mp4-to-mp3): Pull the audio track out of a video file as MP3.
- [M4A to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/m4a-to-mp3): iPhone voice memos and Apple audio into universally playable MP3.
- [WAV to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/wav-to-mp3): Compress a DAW bounce or recording to a shareable MP3.
- [FLAC to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/flac-to-mp3): Turn a lossless archive into something a phone or car will play.
- [AAC to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/aac-to-mp3): For players and car stereos that never learned to read AAC.
- [OGG to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/ogg-to-mp3): Vorbis audio from Discord, Telegram or game files into MP3.
- [Opus / WhatsApp voice note to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/opus-to-mp3): WhatsApp and Signal voice notes into a format anything will open.
- [WMA to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/wma-to-mp3): Old Windows Media libraries into something a Mac or a phone will play.
- [CAF to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/caf-to-mp3): Apple Core Audio files from GarageBand and Logic, made portable.
- [AC3 / Dolby Digital to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/ac3-to-mp3): DVD and broadcast soundtracks, with 5.1 folded down to stereo.
- [MOV to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/mov-to-mp3): Audio out of iPhone and QuickTime recordings.
- [AIFF to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/aiff-to-mp3): Logic and GarageBand bounces compressed for sharing.
- [M4B to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/m4b-to-mp3): Audiobooks out of Apple’s format and onto anything else.

## Other format conversions

- [MP3 to WAV](https://audiosaw.com/mp3-to-wav): Uncompressed PCM for DAW import, CD burning and samplers.
- [MP3 to M4A](https://audiosaw.com/mp3-to-m4a): AAC in an Apple-friendly container for iTunes and CarPlay.
- [MP3 to AIFF](https://audiosaw.com/mp3-to-aiff): Apple-native uncompressed audio for Logic and Final Cut.
- [WAV to FLAC](https://audiosaw.com/wav-to-flac): Lossless compression — same audio, roughly half the size.
- [FLAC to WAV](https://audiosaw.com/flac-to-wav): Decompress lossless audio for software that will not read FLAC.
- [WAV at 44.1 kHz, 16-bit](https://audiosaw.com/wav-44100-16bit): The CD standard, locked in — what most software assumes.
- [WAV to MP3 at 128 kbps](https://audiosaw.com/wav-to-mp3-128kbps): The small-file setting — right for speech, web and email.
- [MP3 at 320 kbps](https://audiosaw.com/mp3-320kbps): The MP3 quality ceiling, locked in.

## Video to audio

- [Extract audio from video](https://audiosaw.com/extract-audio): Any video container to any audio format, without uploading the video.
- [MP4 to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/mp4-to-mp3): Pull the audio track out of a video file as MP3.
- [MOV to MP3](https://audiosaw.com/mov-to-mp3): Audio out of iPhone and QuickTime recordings.

## Cut, trim & arrange

- [Audio Cutter](https://audiosaw.com/audio-cutter): Drag handles on a waveform and keep only the part you want.
- [Audio Joiner](https://audiosaw.com/audio-joiner): Concatenate several files into one, in the order you choose.
- [Ringtone Maker](https://audiosaw.com/ringtone-maker): A 30-second clip from any song, in the format your phone wants.
- [Change audio speed](https://audiosaw.com/audio-speed): Slow a song or speed a podcast without shifting the pitch.
- [Audio Reverser](https://audiosaw.com/audio-reverser): Play a file backwards — for effects, or to hear what is buried.
- [Fade in / fade out](https://audiosaw.com/fade-in-fade-out): Clean fades on both ends without opening an editor.
- [Trim silence off the ends](https://audiosaw.com/trim-silence-edges): Top and tail a recording, leaving the middle untouched.
- [Auto-Cut Silence](https://audiosaw.com/auto-cut-silence): Shorten the pauses between phrases, keeping speech natural.
- [Remove silence](https://audiosaw.com/silence-remover): Strip dead air out of a podcast, voice memo or voiceover.

## Loudness & channels

- [LUFS Loudness Normalizer](https://audiosaw.com/loudness-normalizer): Match the loudness target Spotify, Apple or broadcast expects.
- [Normalize Audio](https://audiosaw.com/normalize-audio): Bring files to a consistent level so nothing jumps out.
- [Amplify quiet audio](https://audiosaw.com/amplify-audio): Make a too-quiet recording usable without driving it into distortion.
- [Compress an audio file](https://audiosaw.com/audio-compressor): Get a file under an email, Discord or upload size limit.
- [Stereo to mono](https://audiosaw.com/stereo-to-mono): Fix one-sided recordings and halve the size of voice files.
- [Mono to stereo](https://audiosaw.com/mono-to-stereo): Honest dual-mono for software that insists on two channels.
- [Change the sample rate](https://audiosaw.com/change-sample-rate): Resample to match a project and stop import warnings.

## Clean up & separate

- [Vocal remover / karaoke](https://audiosaw.com/vocal-remover): Remove the vocal from a stereo song, or isolate it, by cancelling the centre.
- [AI vocal remover / stem splitter](https://audiosaw.com/stem-splitter): Neural separation into a clean instrumental and acapella, running on your machine.
- [Remove background noise](https://audiosaw.com/noise-reduction): Strip hiss, hum and fan noise out of a recording with spectral gating.
- [EQ & bass booster](https://audiosaw.com/audio-eq): Adjust bass, mids and treble, or boost the low end, baked into the file.
- [Autotune / Pitch Correction](https://audiosaw.com/autotune): Snap a vocal to a key — subtle tuning or the hard-tuned effect.
- [Pitch & key changer](https://audiosaw.com/pitch-shifter): Shift the key up or down by semitones without changing the tempo.

## Record & tag

- [Voice recorder](https://audiosaw.com/voice-recorder): Record from your microphone in the browser — the audio never leaves your device.
- [Audio to MIDI](https://audiosaw.com/audio-to-midi): Turn a hummed melody or bassline into a MIDI file.
- [BPM Finder](https://audiosaw.com/bpm-finder): Detect the tempo of a track, with half and double time shown.
- [Split an audio file](https://audiosaw.com/split-audio): Cut one long recording into equal parts, fixed chunks, or at the silent gaps.
- [MP3 tag editor](https://audiosaw.com/mp3-tag-editor): Edit title, artist, album and cover art without re-encoding the audio.

## For a specific app or device

- [Audio for Whisper](https://audiosaw.com/audio-for-whisper): 16 kHz mono WAV — exactly what Whisper wants, in one click.
- [Prep audio for transcription](https://audiosaw.com/audio-to-text-prep): The format each transcription service actually wants.
- [Podcast prep](https://audiosaw.com/podcast-prep): Normalize, mono mixdown and MP3 encode in a single pass.
- [Compress audio for Discord](https://audiosaw.com/discord-audio-compressor): Fits under the upload limit without you doing the maths.
- [Audio for CapCut](https://audiosaw.com/capcut-audio): The format CapCut imports without complaint.
- [Audio for DaVinci Resolve](https://audiosaw.com/davinci-resolve-audio): The format Resolve always imports, no conform errors.
- [M4A to WAV for Audacity](https://audiosaw.com/m4a-to-wav-for-audacity): Skip the FFmpeg install Audacity keeps asking you for.
- [WAV for SP-404 / MPC](https://audiosaw.com/wav-for-sp404): The exact spec hardware samplers need, or they fail silently.
